newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Up on crude rally.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Up on crude rally.

text.p: Singapore oil product swaps rose at midday on the back of the overnight rally in the crude market, brokers said on Tuesday.
Gas oil gained 25-30 cents, fuel oil rose by 50 cents and naphtha by 25 cents after Brent crude futures closed up 50 cents in London to $19.45 per barrel.

Brent hit an intraday high of $19.64 on news of a force majeure declared at Colombia's Cano Limon crude field, the approval of the Iraqi aid distribution plan by the U.N. which saw traders needing to short cover and finding only buyers in the market.
The shutdowns at three catalytic crackers in Northwest Europe and tight supplies of reformulated gasoline also added to the bullish tone.
August gas oil traded earlier in the day at $22.95 per barrel, and was last quoted at $22.80/$23.00, from Monday's $22.55/$22.65.
September was indicated at $23.50/$23.70, from Tuesday's $23.25/$23.35, while October was discussed at $24.00/$24.35.

Traders said aside from the bullish crude, direction on the physical gas oil market was mixed as regional demand remained soft with India taking only two cargoes for September, while China has not emerged to buy large volumes.
Taiwan has emerged to sell for September while Nepal is seeking to buy September gas oil. Some demand has also emerged from the Philippines for September.
Amid the rise in swaps values, physical gas oil traded lower on Monday at $22.50, down 35 cents from the last July 29 trade.
After faltering to as low as 20 cents last week, the August gas oil/jet fuel regrade widened again to be offered at $1.00 with no bids, from Monday's 50/70 cents.
Traders said this was due to more bullish sentiment on jet fuel as the cold season approaches and players begin to stock up as sellers hold out for higher prices.
Physical jet fuel was offered at $23.50 on Monday, 30-50 cents higher than on Friday, but buyers were not impressed.
Fuel oil also rose on the back of crude and tight physical supplies as fresh supplies from the MidEast were absent.
August swaps were bid at $101.75, from Monday's $101.50/$102 per tonne, while September and October was indicated at $102.00/$102.50, from Monday's $101.50/$102.00.
